items.name: Prim's algorithm from A

items.name: Kruskal with fixed arcs; Prim comparison
items.how: (i) Use Kruskal's algorithm to find the minimum spanning tree that includes the existing arcs BC and EF, listing arcs in the order considered and saying whether each is added; (ii) explain why Kruskal is a better choice than Prim in this case.
items.ms: (i) M1 first three arcs CF, AB, FG chosen with at least one rejection seen; 1A1 all six arcs CF, AB, FG, AD, EH, HI selected at the right time (BC and EF ignored); 2A1 cso with every rejection correct and in order. (ii) B1 partial: BC and EF are not connected / the tree starts disconnected; B1 full: Kruskal can build from disconnected fragments whereas Prim needs a connected tree. Describing how to adapt Kruskal scores nothing.

items.ms: (i) B1 n = 1 both sides equal 6; M1 assume true for n = k; M1 add the (k+1)th term; A1 reach (1/4)(k+1)(k+2)(k+3)(k+4) with no errors; A1 cso conclusion. items.ms: B1 for the conjugate root 5 + i.

items.name: Solve quartic completely
items.how: Solve the equation f(z) = 0 completely.
items.ms: M1 forms the quadratic factor from the conjugate pair; A1 z² - 10z + 26; M1 finds the other quadratic factor 2z² + ...z + k (inspection with constant 6, or long division); A1 2z² + z - 6; A1 real roots z = 3/2 and z = -2 (complex roots need not be restated). Parts (b) and (c) are marked together.

deps.name: Conjugate root of quartic

items.name: Find unknown coefficients of quartic
items.how: Determine the value of A and the value of B.
items.ms: M1 multiplies out (z² - 10z + 26)(2z² + z - 6), or extracts the z² and z terms; A1 A = 36, B = 86. Alternative order: substitute 5 + i into f(z) and equate real and imaginary parts to solve for A and B (M1A1M1A1A1), then solve the quartic for the real roots.

deps.name: Solve quartic completely

items.how: Determine (i) α² + β² and (ii) α³ + β³.

items.name: Quadratic with roots α³-β and β³-α

items.ms: M1 attempts the sum (α³ + β³) - (α + β) = -75/8; M1 expands the product (α³ - β)(β³ - α) = (αβ)³ - α⁴ - β⁴ + αβ and uses a correct identity for α⁴ + β⁴ (e.g. (α² + β²)² - 2(αβ)²); A1 product 369/16; M1 applies x² - (sum)x + product; A1 16x² + 150x + 369 = 0 (any integer multiple).

items.name: Sum of (r+1)(r+2) and consecutive products
items.how: No part ids in the input; (a) use the standard results for the sums of r² and r to show that the sum of (r + 1)(r + 2) from r = 0 to n equals (1/3)(n + 1)(n + 2)(n + 3) (5); (b) hence determine 10 × 11 + 11 × 12 + ... + 100 × 101 (3).
items.ms: (a) M1 uses at least one standard formula correctly; A1 A1 for the correct pieces then the fully correct expression ((1/6)n(n + 1)(2n + 1) + (3/2)n(n + 1) + 2n + 2); M1 factorises out (n + 1); A1* cso with an intermediate step shown. (b) B1 upper limit 99; M1 correct strategy: sum to 99 minus sum to 8 using the part (a) result; A1 343070.
path: FP1.7.1 - Summation of simple finite s

items.name: Two inductions: recurrence formula and divisibility
items.how: No part ids in the input; two proofs by induction: (i) u1 = 3 and u(n+1) = 2u(n) - 2^(n+1) (printed as '2n + 1' in the extraction; reconstructed from the scheme) gives u(n) = 5 × 2^(n-1) - n × 2^n (5); (ii) f(n) = 5^(n+2) - 4n - 9 is divisible by 16 (5).
items.ms: (i) B1 n = 1 gives u1 = 3; M1 substitutes the n = k formula into the recurrence to get u(k + 1); A1 correct expanded expression 5 × 2^k - k × 2^(k+1) - 2^(k+1); A1 reaches 5 × 2^k - (k + 1)2^(k+1) with no errors; A1cso full conclusion. (ii) B1 f(1) = 112 = 16 × 7; M1 attempts f(k + 1); dM1 expresses it in terms of f(k); A1 f(k + 1) = 5f(k) + 16k + 32; A1cso full conclusion. Alternatives f(k + 1) - m f(k) or f(k + 1) - f(k) are accepted.

items.name: Inverse of 2x2 matrix in k + Inverse of product using reverse order

items.how: Hence find the equations of the two normals to C passing through (54, 0), in the form y = px + q.
items.ms: M1 substitutes x = 54, y = 0 into the part (a) equation and collects terms (9t³ - 36t = 0); dM1 solves for a non-zero t (t = ±2) and attempts a normal equation; A1 one correct equation in any form; A1 both y = -2x + 108 and y = 2x - 108 in the required form.

items.name: Sum of r^2(r+2) using standard results
items.how: Single 4-mark question whose stem is not in the input; the mark scheme shows a closed form for a sum of r^2(r+2) built from the standard summation results, ending as (1/12)n(n+1)(3n^2+11n+4).

items.name: Cartesian equation of image circle
items.how: T: w = (3iz - 2)/(z + i), z not equal to -i, maps |z + i| = 1 to a circle C in the w-plane; find a cartesian equation of C.
items.ms: M1 A1 make z the subject (z = (wi + 2)/(3i - w) or equivalent), M1 form z + i over a common denominator, M1 A1 set |z + i| = 1, dM1 A1 introduce u and v and use Pythagoras to reach u^2 + (v - 3)^2 = 1. A quicker route writes w = 3i + 1/(z + i), so |w - 3i| = 1.

items.name: Substitution y = xv in second-order equation

items.ms: (a) B1 de Moivre applied; M1 binomial expansion with evaluated coefficients; A1 imaginary terms simplified; M1 equate imaginary parts and replace cos^2 by 1 - sin^2; A1* given result with the (1 - sin^2 θ)^2 expansion shown. (b) M1 x = sin θ so sin 5θ = -1/5; A1 correct value; dM1 arcsin and divide by 5; A1 two values; A1 all five x = -0.963, -0.555, -0.040, 0.620, 0.938 (answers only with no working score nothing, since hence). (c) M1 rewrite integrand using (a) as (sin 5θ - 5 sin θ)/4 - 6 sin θ; A1 integrate; dM1 substitute limits with exact trig values; A1 73√2/20 - 36/5.

(c) M1 auxiliary equation m^2 - m - 2 = 0 and a CF; A1 Ae^(2t) + Be^(-t); M1 PI at^2 + bt + c differentiated twice; dM1 compare coefficients (a = 1, b = -3, c = 2); A1 y = Ae^(2t) + Be^(-t) + t^2 - 3t + 2. items.ms: M1 list terms from r = 2 using the partial fractions, enough at both ends to show cancelling; dM1 extract the non-cancelled terms (at least 4 correct terms, 5/2 counts as 3); A1 5/2 - 2/n - 1/(n+1); M1 common denominator with at least three terms including denominators n and n+1; A1cso (5n^2 - n - 4)/(2n(n+1)).
path: FP2.2.1 - Summation of simple finite s

items.name: Partial fractions of (3r+1)/(r(r-1)(r+1)) + Method of differences with three-term partial fractions + Sum from r = 15 to 20 using result
items.how: Hence determine the exact value of the same series summed from r = 15 (the upper limit is lost in the text; the scheme uses 20).
items.ms: M1 difference of two summations (to 20 minus to 14) using the result of (b) or an earlier form; A1 13/210 exact.
path: FP2.2.1 - Summation of simple finite s

items.name: Transform Euler-type equation using x = e^u + General solution of second-order DE with linear forcing + Revert to general solution in terms of x

items.ms: B1 reverse the substitution u = ln x (no ft): y = Ax^-4 + Bx^2 - (1/2) ln x - 1/8; e^(-4 ln x) and e^(2 ln x) are accepted but y = must be shown.

items.name: Fifth roots of 32i
items.how: Question text is missing from the input (page-continuation stub only). From the mark scheme: solve z^5 - 32i = 0, giving the roots in the form re^(iθ).
items.ms: B1 r = 2; M1 strategy for at least two values of θ (5θ = π/2 + 2nπ, so θ = π/10 + 2nπ/5, initial angle may be wrong); A1ft at least two correct roots; A1 all five: 2e^(iπ/10), 2e^(iπ/2), 2e^(i9π/10), 2e^(i13π/10), 2e^(i17π/10) with r = 2.
path: FP2.3.2 - De Moivres theorem and its a

items.name: Rational inequality with x/(2-x) and (x+3)/x
items.how: Use algebra to determine the set of values of x for which x/(2 - x) <= (x + 3)/x (form read from the scheme); solutions relying entirely on graphical methods are not acceptable.
items.ms: M1 collect to one side; M1 common denominator and A1 correct fraction (x^2 - (2 - x)(x + 3))/(x(2 - x)); B1 critical values 0 and 2; M1 solve the numerator 2x^2 + x - 6 = 0; A1 critical values 3/2 and -2; A1A1 x <= -2, 0 < x <= 3/2, x > 2 (and/or/comma between regions fine, intersection symbol not). Alternative: multiply by x^2(2 - x)^2.

items.name: Image of imaginary axis under Mobius map
items.how: The transformation w = ((2 + i)z + 4)/(z - i), z not equal to i, maps the imaginary axis in the z-plane onto line l in the w-plane. Determine a Cartesian equation of l in the form au + bv + c = 0 with integers a, b, c.
items.ms: M1 make z the subject and A1 z = (wi + 4)/(w - 2 - i); M1 w = u + iv and multiply by the conjugate of the denominator; dM1 set the real part to zero; A1 any correct equation; A1 3u + 2v - 8 = 0 (any integer multiple). Alternatives: z = iy and eliminate y, or map two points of the imaginary axis and find the line.

items.name: Circle locus from ratio of distances
items.how: P represents z with |z + 1 - 13i| = 3|z - 7 - 5i| on an Argand diagram. Given that the locus of P is a circle, determine its centre and radius.
items.ms: M1 Pythagoras on both sides (3 or 9 on the RHS); A1 x^2 + y^2 - 16x - 8y + 62 = 0; A1 centre (8, 4) (A0 if i included); M1 radius from r^2 = 64 + 16 - 62; A1 radius 3√2 exact.
path: FP2.3.3 - Loci and regions in the Arga

items.name: Intersection of circle locus and half-line
items.how: Q represents w with arg(w - 8 - 6i) = -3π/4 on the same diagram. Given that the locus of P meets the locus of Q at R, determine the complex number representing R.
items.ms: B1 convert the half-line to Cartesian form y - 6 = x - 8 (y = x - 2); M1 substitute into the circle equation and solve; A1 one correct coordinate; A1 R = (7 - 2√2) + (5 - 2√2)i, exact, with the other intersection rejected.

deps.name: Circle locus from ratio of distances

items.name: Substitution x = t^2 then solve and revert
items.how: (a) Show that x = t^2 transforms 4x d2y/dx2 + 2(1 + 2x) dy/dx - 15y = 15x (I) into d2y/dt2 + 2 dy/dt - 15y = 15t^2 (II) (5 marks); (b) Solve (II) to determine y in terms of t (5 marks); (c) Hence determine the general solution of (I) (1 mark).
items.ms: (a) M1 chain rule dx/dt = 2t; A1 dy/dx = (1/(2t)) dy/dt; dM1 strategy for d2y/dx2 with chain rule used on at least one term; ddM1 full substitution into (I); A1* cso printed (II). (b) M1 solve m^2 + 2m - 15 = 0; A1 CF Ae^(-5t) + Be^(3t); M1 PI at^2 + bt + c differentiated twice; dM1 compare coefficients (a = -1, b = -4/15, c = -38/225); A1 y = CF - t^2 - (4/15)t - 38/225. (c) B1ft replace t by √x.

items.name: Cardioid-type point with vertical tangent
items.how: Curve C: r = 1 + sin θ, -π/2 < θ <= π/2. The tangent to C at P is perpendicular to the initial line. Use calculus to determine the polar coordinates of P.
items.ms: M1 differentiate r cos θ (product rule or double angle); A1 correct derivative; dM1 set to zero and reach 2 sin^2 θ + sin θ - 1 = 0; ddM1 solve for θ (sin θ = 1/2 or -1); A1 P = (3/2, π/6) with no other answers.

items.name: Area bounded by curve and two tangents
items.how: The tangent at Q (θ = π/2, parallel to the initial line) meets the tangent at P at S. Region R is bounded by the line segments QS, SP and the curve. Use algebraic integration to show the area of R is (1/32)(a√3 + bπ) with a, b integers.
items.ms: M1 (1/2)∫r^2 dθ with sin^2 θ = (1/2)(1 - cos 2θ); A1 correct integration (3θ/2 - 2cos θ - (1/4) sin 2θ); M1 apply limits π/6 (their θ from (a)) and π/2; M1 area of trapezium OQSP; dM1 fully correct method for R, 1/2 included; A1cao (21√3 - 8π)/32.

items.name: Method of differences proof for sum of fourth powers
items.how: (a) Show n^5 - (n - 1)^5 = 5n^4 - 10n^3 + 10n^2 - 5n + 1 (2 marks); (b) Hence, using the method of differences, show that the sum of r^4 from r = 1 to n equals (1/30)n(n + 1)(2n + 1)(an^2 + bn + c) with integers a, b, c (7 marks).
items.ms: (a) M1 expand (n - 1)^5; A1* given result with the full expansion shown. (b) M1 apply (a) for r = 1 to n (at least 3 lines) and sum; A1 n^5 = 5Σr^4 - 10Σr^3 + 10Σr^2 - 5Σr + n; M1 insert at least two standard summation formulae; A1 correct equation; M1 make 5Σr^4 the subject and take out n(n + 1); dM1 take out (2n + 1); A1 (1/30)n(n + 1)(2n + 1)(3n^2 + 3n - 1).
path: FP2.2.1 - Summation of simple finite s

items.name: First-order linear DE with factor x+1
items.how: Whole question (parts a, b): Determine the general solution of (x + 1) dy/dx - xy = e^(3x), x > -1, giving y = f(x).
items.ms: (a) B1 rearrange to dy/dx - xy/(x+1) = e^(3x)/(x+1); M1 strategy for the IF including integrating -x/(x+1) = -1 + 1/(x+1); A1 -x + ln(x+1); A1 IF = (x+1)e^(-x); M1 yI = ∫QI dx; A1 y(x+1)e^(-x) = e^(2x)/2  | (b) M1 substitute x = 0, y = 5 to find c (c = 9/2); A1cao y = e^(3x)/(2(x+1)) + 9e^x/(2(x+1)) with y = shown.

items.name: Third derivative of tan^2 x + Taylor series of tan^2 x about π/3

items.name: Integral using x = 4 cosh θ substitution

items.ms: M1 full attempt at the substitution (dx = 4 sinh θ dθ); M1 simplify (16cosh^2 θ - 16)^(3/2) to k sinh^3 θ; A1 integral of 1/(16 sinh^2 θ) dθ; dM1 integrate to k coth θ; dM1 substitute back (cosh θ = x/4, sinh θ = √(x^2/16 - 1)); A1 -x/(16√(x^2 - 16)) + c, so a = -1/16.

items.how: The line l crosses the x-axis at Q. Show that QF/PF = e where e is the eccentricity of E.

items.ms: M1 apply the reduction formula once to write I_5 in terms of I_3; M1 apply it again to reach I_1 (slips on coefficients allowed); A1 any correct expression in x only; A1 (1/5)√(x^2 + 3)(x^4 - 4x^2 + 24) + k, so p = -4, q = 24. Common loss: omitting the ends gives (pi/2)(4 - 2 sqrt2), about 6/8.

items.name: Eccentricity of ellipse + Foci and directrices of ellipse
items.how: Hence determine (i) the coordinates of the foci and (ii) the equations of the directrices of the ellipse.
items.ms: B1ft foci (+/- ae, 0) = (+/- sqrt5, 0) as coordinates; B1ft directrices x = +/- a/e = +/- 9/sqrt5 (equations, not just values); both follow through their e. Using a^2, b^2 consistently scores B marks as a special case.

items.name: Derivative involving arcsin 2x, then evaluate
items.how: Question text not captured in the input; from the scheme it is a differentiate-then-'hence' pair: differentiate a function whose derivative is 3 arcsin 2x + 6x/sqrt(1 - 4x^2) (product of x and arcsin 2x), then hence find the exact value of dy/dx at x = 1/4.
items.ms: M1 differentiate arcsin(kx) as 1/sqrt(1 - ...) times k and combine by the product rule; A1 correct derivative 3 arcsin 2x + 6x/sqrt(1 - 4x^2); B1 dependent on full marks in the first part: dy/dx = pi/2 + sqrt3 at x = 1/4. 'arsinh' or 'arcsinh' in place of arcsin scores M0.

items.name: Other directrix of hyperbola
items.how: Hyperbola x^2/a^2 - y^2/b^2 = 1 with one directrix given; write down an equation of the other directrix.
items.ms: B1 for the symmetric directrix x = -4/3 (the negative of the given x = 4/3), any equivalent equation.

items.name: Find a and foci of hyperbola
items.how: Determine (i) the value of a and (ii) the coordinates of each focus, given the hyperbola's equation (b^2 = 5) and a directrix x = 4/3.
items.ms: (i) M1 use a/e = 4/3 with b^2 = a^2(e^2 - 1) to form an equation in a (or e); dM1 solve the resulting 3TQ in a^2 (9a^4 - 16a^2 - 80 = 0) to a positive root; A1 a = 2 (e = 3/2) with negative rejected. (ii) M1 numerical ae (or sqrt(a^2 + b^2)); A1 foci (+/-3, 0). Part (ii) can be answered before (i).

items.name: Solve 4 tanh x minus sech x equals 1
items.how: Solve 4 tanh x - sech x = 1, giving the answer as x = ln k with k a fully simplified rational number.
items.ms: M1 replace a hyperbolic function by its exponential form (or convert to sinh and cosh); M1 A1 obtain the correct quadratic 3e^(2x) - 2e^x - 5 = 0; M1 solve for e^x (any exact form including the positive root); A1 x = ln(5/3) with no unrejected extra solutions. Squaring routes (in sinh, tanh, sech or cosh) are also credited but must reject the spurious root.
path: FP3.1.1 - Definition of the six hyperb

items.name: Integral giving arsinh then definite integral
items.how: Single question with two linked parts: (a) determine the integral of 1/sqrt(9x^2 + 16) dx; (b) hence determine the exact value of a definite integral of the same integrand (limits -2 to 2 per the scheme), in the form a ln(b + c sqrt13) with rational a, b, c.
items.ms: (a) M1 obtains p arsinh(qx) (or ln form); A1 (1/3) arsinh(3x/4) + c (arcsin or arsin is M0). (b) M1 substitute limits 2 and -2 into the antiderivative and subtract; dM1 reach a ln-form with sqrt13; A1 (2/3) ln(3/2 + sqrt13/2) or equivalent. Decimal answers are not enough.

items.name: Value of a making matrix singular
items.how: For a 3x3 matrix A containing a positive constant a, determine the exact value of a for which A is singular.
items.ms: The mark scheme in the input does not contain a matching part: its Q5 layout is (a)(i) value of a given eigenvalue 2, (a)(ii) other eigenvalues, (b) eigenvectors, (c) diagonalising P and D, so it appears to belong to the version before the question was reissued. The wording supports setting det A = 0 to get a quadratic in a and taking the positive root, but no marking points are given.

items.name: Find a and other eigenvalues
items.how: Given that 2 is an eigenvalue of A, determine (i) the value of a and (ii) the other two eigenvalues.
items.ms: (i) M1 form det(A - 2I) (or Ax = 2x); dM1 solve the quadratic a^2 + 3a - 10 = 0; A1 a = 2 (a = -5 rejected as a > 0). (ii) M1 characteristic equation with a = 2 giving a real non-zero eigenvalue; A1 eigenvalues 4 and 5 (cubic is lambda^3 - 11lambda^2 + 38lambda - 40 = 0).

items.name: Normalised eigenvectors for other eigenvalues
items.how: Given a normalised eigenvector for eigenvalue 2, determine a normalised eigenvector for each of the other two eigenvalues of A.
items.ms: M1 use Ax = lambda x with their a and a non-zero eigenvalue (not 2) to get three equations (or a cross product of two rows of A - lambda I); A1 one correct eigenvector, A1 both ((0, -1, 2) for 4 and (1, -2, 7) for 5); M1 normalise at least one; A1 both normalised: (1/sqrt5)(0, -1, 2) and (1/sqrt54)(1, -2, 7).

deps.name: Find a and other eigenvalues

items.name: Show sum of squared derivatives for cycloid
items.how: For the curve x = a(t - sin t), y = a(1 - cos t) (a > 0), show that (dx/dt)^2 + (dy/dt)^2 = k a^2 sin^2(t/2) with k to be found.
items.ms: B1 at least one correct derivative; M1 square and add using cos^2 + sin^2 = 1 to get an expression in cos t; dM1 replace cos t by 1 - 2sin^2(t/2); A1 4a^2 sin^2(t/2), k = 4.

items.name: Surface area of revolution of cycloid arch
items.how: The curve from t = 0 to t = 2pi is rotated through 2pi about the x-axis; determine the surface area in terms of pi and a, with no calculator-based integration.
items.ms: M1 apply S = 2pi times the integral of y sqrt(...) dt using the part (a) result with a square root giving p sin(t/2); dM1 trig identities to arguments of t/2 only, giving sin^3(t/2); A1ft correct antiderivative -2cos(t/2) + (2/3)cos^3(t/2) times 8 pi a^2; ddM1 limits 0 and 2pi; A1 (64/3) pi a^2.

deps.name: Show sum of squared derivatives for cycloid

items.name: Angle between line and plane to nearest degree
items.how: Line l passes through (1, 0, 1) and meets the plane at (1, 2, 3); determine the acute angle between plane and line to the nearest degree.
items.ms: B1 direction of l as (0, 2, 2); M1 scalar product of normal and direction divided by the product of magnitudes; A1ft correct numerical expression (value 0.4029...); A1 awrt 24 degrees (acute angle with the plane is 90 minus the angle to the normal, 66.24). Credit for the vector-product (sine) route requires the modulus.

Alternatives: project a vector from a plane point onto the normal, or find the foot of the perpendicular. Work from (b) earns nothing unless used.

items.name: Reduction formula for integral of cos^n x
items.how: With I_n the integral of cos^n x, prove I_n = (1/n) cos^(n-1)x sin x + ((n-1)/n) I_(n-2) for n >= 2.
items.ms: M1 split cos^n as cos x times cos^(n-1)x; dM1 integrate by parts to p sin x cos^(n-1)x + q integral of cos^(n-2)x sin^2 x; A1 replace sin^2 by 1 - cos^2 to get I_n in terms of I_n and I_(n-2); A1* rearrange to the given result with at least one intermediate step and no bracketing errors.
path: FP3.4.5 - The derivation and use of si

items.name: Foci and directrices of ellipse x^2+9y^2=9
items.how: For the ellipse x^2 + 9y^2 = 9, (i) determine the coordinates of the two foci and (ii) write down the equation of each directrix.
items.ms: M1 b^2 = a^2(1 - e^2) with a = 3, b = 1; A1 e = 2sqrt2/3; B1 foci (+/-2sqrt2, 0); B1ft directrices x = +/-9/(2 sqrt2) = +/-9 sqrt2/4 as single fractions (x = a/e). Not a follow-through mark for the foci.

items.name: Sum of focal distances equals 6
items.how: For a general point P on the ellipse, show that PF1 + PF2 = 6.
items.ms: M1 state the focus-directrix definition PF = e PM (or use a general point P with distance formulas); dM1 PF1 + PF2 = e(PM1 + PM2) with e and the directrices from (a), or the parametric/Cartesian distance route; A1* fully correct proof valid for any P. Using one specific P or just 2a = 6 scores 0.

items.name: Locus of midpoint of chord is line
items.how: The line y = 2x + c through P meets the ellipse again at Q and M is the midpoint of PQ; show that as P varies the locus of M is a straight line through the origin.
items.ms: M1 substitute the line into the ellipse; A1 correct quadratic 37x^2 + 36cx + 9c^2 - 9 = 0; dM1 A1 x-coordinate of M as half the sum of roots (x = -18c/37); ddM1 eliminate c using y = 2x + c to get an equation in x and y only; A1* y = -x/18 with a conclusion that it passes through the origin.

items.name: Even-power cosine integral product formula + Evaluate cos^6 x sin^2 x integral
items.how: Hence determine the exact value of the integral from 0 to pi/2 of cos^6 x sin^2 x dx.
items.ms: M1 replace sin^2 x by 1 - cos^2 x (or attempt I_6 - I_8); A1 correct numerical expression using part (b) for I_6 and I_8; A1 5pi/256. Must be clear use of I_6 - I_8 from (b): answer alone scores 0/3.
path: FP3.4.5 - The derivation and use of si

items.name: Two integrals giving arctan and arcsin
items.how: Question text not captured in the input; from the scheme it is two unrelated parts: (i) evaluate exactly a definite integral of 8/(16 + x^2) (limits 4 to 4 sqrt3), (ii) given a definite integral of 2/sqrt(9 - 4x^2) up to an unknown upper limit k has value pi/12, find k.
items.ms: (i) M1 obtains arctan(x/4) form with coefficient 2; dM1 substitute limits and subtract; A1 pi/6. (ii) M1 A1 obtain arcsin(2x/3) (fully correct integration); dM1 substitute limits, set the result equal to pi/12 and solve for k with correct order of operations; A1 k = 3 sqrt2 / 4. Common wrong answer k = 0.913 from mis-integrating the arcsin term.

items.name: Find unknowns in matrix inverse pair

items.ms: M1 multiply TU (or UT) and obtain at least two equations with one correct; dM1 solve for two of the constants; A1 two correct values; A1 all three correct: a = 2, b = 9, c = -4. Alternative: equate T^-1 elements to U.

items.name: Cartesian equation of line before transformation
items.how: Matrix T maps line l1 onto line l2 given in Cartesian form; determine a Cartesian equation for l1.
items.ms: M1 write l2 in vector/parametric form (position and direction); M1 multiply by U = T^-1 (with b and c from (a)) to get the position and direction of l1, or solve Tx = point and Tx = direction; dM1 convert to Cartesian form; A1 (x - 14)/18 = (y - 33)/52 = (z + 18)/(-27) or equivalent.

deps.name: Find unknowns in matrix inverse pair

items.name: Foci and directrices in terms of e
items.how: Ellipse x^2/49 + y^2/b^2 = 1 (0 < b < 7) with eccentricity e; write down in terms of e only (i) the foci and (ii) the directrices.
items.ms: B1 foci (+/-7e, 0); B1 directrices x = +/-7/e. Special case: consistently using 49 for 7 scores B0 B1.

items.name: Find e from y-intercept
items.how: Given the ellipse crosses the y-axis at (0, +/-4 sqrt3), determine the value of e.
items.ms: M1 replace b^2 by (4 sqrt3)^2 = 48 and solve 48 = 49(1 - e^2) for e^2 or e; A1 e = 1/7 (not +/-).

deps.name: Show b^2 = 49(1 - e^2) from focus-directrix

items.name: Area of triangle OPM
items.how: Given the x-coordinate of P (7/2 per the scheme), determine the area of triangle OPM where O is the origin.
items.ms: M1 substitute x = 7/2 into the ellipse with b^2 = 48 to get y = 6 (y^2 = 36); dM1 area as half base PM (directrix x = 7/e = 49, so PM = 49 - 7/2) times height y (or shoelace); A1 273/2. Using the wrong ellipse denominator (y^2 = 36 from the special case) scores M0 M1 A0.

deps.name: Find e from y-intercept

items.name: Prove tanh identity and tanh^n reduction formula
items.how: Single question with an internal chain: (a) use exponential definitions to prove 1 - sech^2 x = tanh^2 x (3 marks); (b) for I_n = integral of tanh^n 3x dx from 0 to (1/3) ln 2, show I_n = I_(n-2) - p^(n-1)/(3(n-1)) with p rational (4 marks); (c) hence find the exact value of the integral of tanh^5 3x over the same limits as a ln b + c (4 marks).
items.ms: (a) B1 replace sech x by 2/(e^x + e^-x); M1 single fraction and expand numerator; A1* reach (e^x - e^-x)^2/(e^x + e^-x)^2. (b) M1 write tanh^n = tanh^(n-2)(1 - sech^2); dM1 integrate tanh^(n-2) 3x sech^2 3x to tanh^(n-1) 3x/(3(n-1)); ddM1 apply limit using tanh(ln 2) = 3/5; A1 p = 3/5. (c) M1 use the reduction formula twice to I_1; M1 integrate tanh 3x to q ln cosh 3x; ddM1 apply the limit with cosh(ln 2) = 5/4; A1 (1/3) ln(5/4) - 177/2500.

items.name: Differentiate arccos(sech x)
items.how: Given y = arccos(sech x) for x > 0, show that dy/dx = sech x.
items.ms: M1 take cos of both sides and differentiate implicitly to get -sin y dy/dx = -sech x tanh x; dM1 use correct identities (sin y = tanh x) to get an equation in x only with no roots; A1* fully correct proof. Clear errors such as treating d/dx(sech x) as +sech x tanh x score A0.

items.name: Minimum point of arccos sech plus coth
items.how: P is the minimum point of y = arccos(sech x) + coth x for x > 0; show that its x-coordinate is ln(q + sqrt(q^2 - 1)) with q involving sqrt k, k an integer.
items.ms: B1 derivative of coth x (-cosech^2 x); M1 set f'(x) = 0 using part (a) and identities to get a 3TQ in cosh x or sech x; A1 cosh^2 x - cosh x - 1 = 0 (or sech form); dM1 solve for an exact value > 1; ddM1 apply the log form of arcosh; A1 x = ln((1 + sqrt5)/2 + sqrt(((1 + sqrt5)/2)^2 - 1)), k = 5. Giving cosh x = (1 + sqrt5)/2 with no source scores B1 M1 A1 dM1 only.

deps.name: Differentiate arccos(sech x)

items.name: Perimeter of region as integral for parabola
items.how: Region R is bounded by y^2 = 8x and the line x = 18; show that the perimeter is alpha + 2 times the integral from 0 to beta of sqrt(1 + y^2/16) dy, with alpha and beta found (all stages of working shown).
items.ms: B1 dx/dy = y/4; M1 form sqrt(1 + (dx/dy)^2) dy correctly; A1 perimeter = 24 + 2 integral from 0 to 12 of sqrt(1 + y^2/16) dy, using y = +/-12 at x = 18 and symmetry about the x-axis.

Column order must match D.

items.name: Differentiate arctan 2x/3 then integrate by parts
items.how: Question text not captured in the input; from the scheme it has two parts: (a) differentiate y = arctan(2x/3) (2 marks), (b) integrate arctan(2x/3) with respect to x (4 marks), using part (a) in the follow-through.
items.ms: (a) M1 derivative of arctan(qx) as p/(1 + (qx)^2) with brackets around qx; A1 6/(9 + 4x^2). (b) M1 integration by parts the correct way round, A1ft using their part (a) result; M1 integrate x/(9 + 4x^2) as a ln term; A1 x arctan(2x/3) - (3/4) ln(9 + 4x^2) + c (the +c is not required).

items.name: Ellipse directrix giving two values of a
items.how: The line x = 9 is a directrix of the ellipse x^2/a^2 + y^2/8 = 1 (a > 0); find the two possible exact values of a (the 8 is taken from the scheme).
items.ms: B1 both equations a/e = 9 and a^2(1 - e^2) = 8; M1 A1 eliminate to a quadratic in a^2 (a^4 - 81a^2 + 648 = 0) or in e^2, with terms collected; M1 solve the quadratic for a^2 or e^2; M1 A1 complete method to a, using a = 9e at least once, giving a = 3 and a = 6 sqrt2. Do not accept +/- unless the negative is rejected.

items.name: Prove cosh^2 - sinh^2 = 1 by exponentials
items.how: Using the definitions of sinh x and cosh x in terms of exponentials, prove cosh^2 x - sinh^2 x = 1.
items.ms: M1 correct exponential forms for cosh and sinh with both brackets squared (three terms each); A1 at least one line of intermediate working (common denominator) with no errors, concluding 4/4 = 1.

items.name: Solve 2 sinh x + 7 cosh x = 9

items.ms: M1 differentiate and substitute x = 0 for gradient 126, A1ft l: y = 126x - 360, dM1 set equal to the cubic, ddM1 solve a cubic of the form ax^3 + bx^2 = 0 by taking out x^2, A1 x = -67/6 (x = 0 ignored). An error in the x coefficient of the expansion in (b) can be fully recovered here.

deps.name: Expand three linear brackets

items.name: Normal equation from tangent equation
items.how: Curve C: y = f(x), x > 0 with f''(x) = 4x + x^(-1/2) (index partly lost in the input); P has x coordinate 4 and the tangent at P is y = 3x + 4; find an equation of the normal at P.
items.ms: M1 for stating or implying the normal gradient -1/3, A1 for a correct full equation, e.g. y - 16 = -(1/3)(x - 4); the y coordinate 16 comes from the tangent equation, and (y - 16)/(x - 4) = -1/3 is not accepted as an equation.

items.name: Integrate second derivative twice for f
items.how: Find f(x), in simplest form, given f''(x) = 4x + x^(-1/2), f'(4) = 3 (tangent gradient) and f(4) = 16 (point P).
items.ms: M1 integrate f'' once (one index correct), dM1 use f'(4) = 3 to find the constant -33, A1 f'(x) = 2x^2 + 2x^(1/2) - 33, dM1 integrate again, ddM1 use f(4) = 16 for the second constant, A1 f(x) = (2/3)x^3 + (4/3)x^(3/2) - 33x + 284/3. Work for this part may be seen in (a).

deps.name: Normal equation from tangent equation

path: P1.5.2 - Integration of xn and relate

items.name: Reduce exponential equation to quadratic in p + Solve exponential equation via quadratic
items.how: Hence solve 3*9^x + 3^(x+2) = 1 + 3^(x-1) (non-calculator, all stages).
items.ms: M1 for a valid non-calculator solution of 9p^2 + 26p - 3 = 0 (answers written down score M0), A1 (M1 on e-pen) for 3^x = 1/9 clearly stated as a value of 3^x (3^x = -3 can be ignored), A1 for x = -2 only.

items.name: Radius of sector from area + Angle AOB from straight line + Total area of stage
items.how: Hence find the total area of the stage in m^2 to 1 d.p. (sector plus two triangles with sides 5.77 m and 6.25 m).
items.ms: M1 for the area of triangle AOB = (1/2)(5.77)(6.25)sin(0.37), dM1 for full method 40 + 2*triangle, A1 for awrt 53.1 (53.0 condoned). Degree working is allowed but part (b) must be in radians.
path: P1.3.1 - The sine and cosine rules, a

items.name: Radius of sector from area + Angle AOB from straight line + Total area of stage + Total perimeter of stage
items.how: Hence find the total perimeter of the stage in m to 1 d.p.
items.ms: M1 for the arc length r*theta = 5.77*2.4, M1 for the cosine rule to find AB (or CD), ddM1 for the full perimeter 12.5 + 2AB + arc, A1 for awrt 30.9. Taking AB = 6.25sin(0.37) (right-angle assumption) is a common error giving M1 M0 ddM0 A0.
path: P1.3.1 - The sine and cosine rules, a

items.name: Expand cubic product then integrate
items.how: Single question (stem text missing from the input, reconstructed from the scheme): find the integral of (2x - 5)(3x + 2)(2x + 5) with respect to x.
items.ms: M1 multiply two brackets to a quadratic and then the third, A1 12x^3 + 8x^2 - 75x - 50, M1 integrate with an index raised and processed, A1ft two correct collected terms, A1 3x^4 + (8/3)x^3 - (75/2)x^2 - 50x + c; the +c is required and clearing fractions after a correct answer is not ignored.
path: P1.5.2 - Integration of xn and relate

items.name: Sin of angle from triangle area
items.how: Triangle ABC with AB = 15 cm, AC = 25 cm, angle BAC = theta degrees and area 100 cm^2; find the value of sin(theta).
items.ms: M1 for area = (1/2)ab sin C with the given data (slips condoned), A1 for sin(theta) = 8/15 or an exact equivalent fraction; finishing with sin C = 8/15 is A0 but later marks are still available.
path: P1.3.1 - The sine and cosine rules, a

items.name: Cosine rule with obtuse angle
items.how: Given that theta > 90, find the length of BC in cm to 3 s.f.
items.ms: M1 cosine rule 15^2 + 25^2 - 2(15)(25)cos(angle) using an angle from their part (a), dM1 full cosine rule with the obtuse angle 180 - 32.2, A1 cso awrt 38.5. Using the acute angle (BC about 14.7) loses dM1 and A1; using radians for a degree-labelled angle is a special case M1 dM1 A0.

deps.name: Sin of angle from triangle area

path: P1.3.1 - The sine and cosine rules, a

items.name: Differentiate algebraic fraction as power terms
items.how: Curve C: y = (5x^3 - 8)/(2x^2), x > 0 (reconstructed from the scheme); find dy/dx, giving the answer in simplest form.
items.ms: M1 write y as a sum of two terms with at least one correct index ((5/2)x - 4x^(-2)), dM1 both indices correct and differentiated (Px + Qx^(-2) to A + Bx^(-3)), A1 one correct term, A1 5/2 + 8x^(-3) or 5/2 + 8/x^3. A quotient-rule route is accepted, earning the first two marks together.
path: P1.4.2 - Differentiation of xn, and r

items.name: Tangent equation in integer form
items.how: P(2, 4) lies on C; find an equation of the tangent to C at P in the form ax + by + c = 0 where a, b and c are integers.
items.ms: M1 substitute x = 2 into their dy/dx (not into y) to get the gradient 7/2, M1 y - 4 = m(x - 2) with their numerical gradient (y = mx + c must reach c), A1 7x - 2y - 6 = 0 or any integer multiple. A gradient from a calculator with no working earns only the last M1 A1.

deps.name: Differentiate algebraic fraction as power terms

items.name: Equation of line through two points
items.how: Line l1 passes through P(-2, 9) and Q(10, 6); find its equation in the form y = mx + c (show all stages, no calculator).
items.ms: M1 gradient as change in y over change in x the right way up, dM1 line through a point with their gradient and coordinates in the correct places, A1 y = -(1/4)x + 17/2 in the form y = mx + c. A simultaneous-equation route (9 = -2m + c, 6 = 10m + c) is also accepted.
path: Topic 2 Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane

items.ms: B1ft l2: y = 4x (negative reciprocal of their gradient), M1 solve their l2 and l1 simultaneously by a non-calculator route (some working visible), A1 one correct coordinate, A1 R = (2, 8). Answers with no or insufficient working lose marks.

items.name: Minimum point of cosine graph
items.how: From the graph of y = 5cos(x) (x in degrees), state the coordinates of the minimum point P.

path: P1.3.3 - Sine, cosine and tangent fun

items.name: Maximum point of transformed cosine curves
items.how: Find the coordinates of the maximum point with smallest x > 0 on (i) y = 5cos(x) - 2 and (ii) y = -5cos(x).
items.ms: (i) B1 B1 for (360, 3); (ii) B1 B1 for (180, 5); one mark per correct coordinate (B0 B1 is not possible). Flipped coordinates earn B1 B0; radians or missing brackets cost a mark the first time.
path: P1.3.3 - Sine, cosine and tangent fun

items.name: Reciprocal curve sketch and line non-intersection
items.how: (a) Sketch y = 4/(x - k), k > 0, showing axis intercepts and the vertical asymptote; (b) given that the line y = 9 - x does not cross or touch the curve, find the range of values of k.
items.ms: (a) M1 decreasing branch in quadrant 1, A1 correct shape and position (quadrants 1, 3 and 4), B1 y-intercept (0, -4/k) on the negative y-axis, B1 asymptote x = k. (b) M1 equate to form a quadratic, A1 x^2 - (9 + k)x + 9k + 4 = 0, dM1 discriminant < 0, ddM1 solve k^2 - 18k + 65 and take the inside region, A1 cso 5 < k < 13 (not the outside region).

items.name: Show length AO using arc length
items.how: Platform made of sector DOC and a larger-angle sector AOBEA, both centre O: angle AOB = 0.8 rad, arc CD = 9 m, DA : AO = 3 : 5; show that AO = 7.03 m to 3 s.f.
items.ms: M1 s = r*theta with s = 9, theta = 0.8, A1 OD = 11.25, A1* AO = (5/8)(11.25) = 7.03 with the method visible (7.03125 may be used later). Show-that: the method must be explicit.

items.name: Perimeter of compound sector platform
items.how: Find the perimeter of the platform in m to 3 s.f.
items.ms: M1 major arc AEB = 7.03(2pi - 0.8) (about 38.6), M1 add the pieces 9 + 2(11.25 - 7.03) + arc AEB, A1 awrt 56.0 (56 condoned after correct working).

deps.name: Show length AO using arc length

items.name: Area of compound sector platform
items.how: Find the total area of the platform, in m^2, to the nearest whole number.
items.ms: M1 one sector area ((1/2)(11.25)^2(0.8) = 50.6 or (1/2)(7.03)^2(2pi - 0.8) = 135.4), dM1 add the two sectors, A1 awrt 186.

deps.name: Show length AO using arc length

items.name: Sketch quadratic with given maximum
items.how: C1: y = f(x) is a quadratic with maximum turning point (2, 20) passing through the origin; sketch C1 showing where it cuts the coordinate axes.
items.ms: B1 for an n-shaped quadratic through the origin (quadrants 3, 1 and 4), B1 for the second x-intercept (4, 0) marked on the positive x-axis ((0, 4) is B0).

items.name: Find quadratic from turning point
items.how: Find an expression for f(x), the quadratic with maximum (2, 20) through the origin.
items.ms: M1 form y = Ax(x - 4) or 20 - C(x - 2)^2 (or three equations in ax^2 + bx + c), dM1 find A or C from a given point, A1 -5x(x - 4) = -5x^2 + 20x or 20 - 5(x - 2)^2; may be seen in (c).

deps.name: Sketch quadratic with given maximum

items.name: Intersection of cubic and quadratic
items.how: C2: y = x(x^2 - 4) meets C1 at the origin, P and Q (P has negative x coordinate); using algebra and showing all stages, find the coordinates of P.
items.ms: M1 set x(x^2 - 4) equal to their quadratic through the origin, dM1 expand to px^3 + qx^2 + rx = 0 and take out the factor x, ddM1 solve the quadratic x^2 + 5x - 24 = 0 (calculator allowed), A1 x = -8 chosen (0 and 3 rejected), A1 P = (-8, -480). All stages are required so omissions are penalised.

deps.name: Find quadratic from turning point

items.name: Find k from second derivative zero
items.how: Show all stages: curve C: y = f(x), x > 0 passes through P(2, 8root2), f'(x) = 4x^(3/2) + k/x^2 (reconstructed from the scheme) and f''(x) = 0 at P; find the exact value of k.
items.ms: M1 differentiate f' with at least one index correct, A1 f''(x) = 6x^(1/2) - 2k*x^(-3), dM1 set f''(2) = 0 and solve for k, A1 k = 24root2 (exact). Integrating in (a) or differentiating in (b) earns nothing.
path: P1.4.2 - Differentiation of xn, and r

items.name: Integrate to find f using point
items.how: Find f(x), giving the answer in simplest form, using f'(x) with your value of k and the point P(2, 8root2).
items.ms: M1 integrate f' with one index correct, A1ft (8/5)x^(5/2) - k*x^(-1) (follow through their k), dM1 use P to find c as a multiple of root2, A1 f(x) = (8/5)x^(5/2) - 24root2/x + 68root2/5 or any simplified equivalent.

deps.name: Find k from second derivative zero

path: P1.5.2 - Integration of xn and relate

items.name: Reduce exponential equation to quadratic in p + Solve exponential equation via quadratic
items.how: Hence solve 2*4^x - 2^(x+3) = 17*2^(x-1) - 4 (non-calculator).
items.ms: M1 for a valid non-calculator solution of 4p^2 - 33p + 8 = 0 with working shown ((4p - 1)(p - 8)), M1 for solving 2^x = k for x (logs allowed if k is not a power of 2), A1 for both x = -2 and x = 3. Roots written straight from a calculator score M0.

items.name: Differentiate power terms and find tangent
items.how: Single question (stem text missing from the input): (a) differentiate a curve given as power terms with fractional and negative indices; (b) find the equation of the tangent at the point where x = 4.
items.ms: (a) M1 reduce a correct power by one, A1 one correct simplified term, A1 dy/dx = (3/8)x^2 + 12x^(-3/2) or equivalent (isw). (b) M1 substitute x = 4 into their derivative (gradient 7.5), M1 tangent through the point at x = 4 with their numerical gradient (y = mx + c must reach c), A1 y = 7.5x - 33. A gradient found by calculator with no working still allows the last two marks.

items.name: Integrate quotient with square root
items.how: Find the integral of (4x^2 + 1)/(2*root x) with respect to x, giving the answer in its simplest form.
items.ms: M1 write as a sum of two terms with an index processed, A1 2x^(3/2) + (1/2)x^(-1/2), M1 raise a correct index by one, A1 one correct simplified term, A1 (4/5)x^(5/2) + x^(1/2) + c (the +c is needed; unprocessed indices lose marks).
path: P1.5.2 - Integration of xn and relate

items.name: Area of major sector
items.how: Shape ABCDA is a sector ABCOA (radius 6 cm, with angle AOD = 0.7 rad removed) joined to a triangle AOD; find the area of the sector to 1 d.p.
items.ms: M1 use (1/2)r^2*theta with r = 6 and any allowable angle, M1 correct attempt with the reflex angle 2pi - 0.7 (awrt 100 or 101 accepted for this mark), A1 awrt 100.5. A degree method is allowed if the angle is awrt 40 or 320.

items.name: Normal to curve from derivative
items.how: Curve y = f(x), x > 0 passes through P(4, 1) with f'(x) = 4x^(1/2) - 2 - 8/(3x^2) (reconstructed from the scheme); find the equation of the normal at P in the form ax + by + c = 0 with integer a, b, c.
items.ms: M1 substitute x = 4 into f'(x) (value 35/6), dM1 perpendicular gradient -6/35, M1 normal through (4, 1) with the changed gradient (one sign slip condoned), A1 6x + 35y - 59 = 0 (any positive integer multiple).

items.name: Integrate derivative to find f
items.how: Find f(x) from f'(x) and the point P(4, 1) on the curve.
items.ms: M1 raise a correct index by one (processed), A1 any two terms correct, A1 all three simplified (8/3)x^(3/2) - 2x + 8/(3x), dM1 substitute x = 4, y = 1 to find c, A1 f(x) = (8/3)x^(3/2) - 2x + 8/(3x) - 13. Differentiating f'(x) in (a) and integrating back in (b) earns nothing.
path: P1.5.2 - Integration of xn and relate

items.name: Minimum point of 4 sin
items.how: State the coordinates of the minimum point of y = 4 sin(theta) for 0 <= theta <= 360 degrees (Figure 3 shows the graph).
items.ms: B1 for either coordinate correct (270 or -4, swapped order condoned for this mark), B1 for (270, -4) with or without the degree symbol.
path: P1.3.3 - Sine, cosine and tangent fun

items.name: Point where cubic touches x-axis
items.how: Curve y = f(x) with f(x) = (x - 4)(2x + 1)^2 (as reconstructed from the scheme) touches the x-axis at P and crosses at Q; state the coordinates of P.
items.ms: B1 for P = (-1/2, 0), the repeated root. If both (4, 0) and (-1/2, 0) are given, P must be identified.

items.name: Horizontal translation through the origin
items.how: The curve y = f(x + a), a a constant, passes through the origin; state the possible values of a.
items.ms: B1 for one correct value (f(a) = 0, so a is an x-intercept of f), B1 for both a = -1/2 and a = 4 and no others, given as values (not 'x = ...'). Writing y = f(x - 1/2) or y = f(x + 4) implies the first mark only.

deps.name: Point where cubic touches x-axis

path: P1.1.12 - Knowledge of the effect of s

items.name: Rationalise denominator with surd + Solve linear equation with surd coefficients
items.how: Hence, or otherwise, solve 4x = 2root2*x + 20root2, giving x in the form p + q*root2 with p and q rational.
items.ms: M1 collect the x terms on one side and the constant on the other, dM1 x = 20root2 times the result of (a) (i.e. dividing by 4 - 2root2), A1 10root2 + 10 (10 + 10root2); the A1 cannot be earned without the use of the part (a) value. Squaring or repeating the rationalisation are accepted alternatives with the same marks.
path: P1.1.2 - Use and manipulation of surd

items.name: Perimeter inequality for garden + Area inequality leading to quadratic + Combine inequalities for range of x
items.how: Hence state the range of possible values of x.
items.ms: B1 for 1.5 < x < 2 (or x > 1.5 and x < 2); 'or' between the two inequalities is B0.
path: P1.1.9 - Solutions of linear and quad

items.name: Solve cubic by factorising out x + Solve higher-power equation by substitution
items.how: Hence find all real solutions of an equation of the same form as (a) in terms of (y - 5), with even powers (y - 5)^6, (y - 5)^4 and (y - 5)^2 as read from the scheme.
items.ms: B1 y = 5 stated as a solution, M1 recognise (y - 5)^2 equals a positive root from (a) (7/2) and solve for y, A1ft one solution of the form 5 +/- root(7/2) (decimals allowed for this mark only), A1 both 5 + root(7/2) and 5 - root(7/2) in exact form, no complex or extra solutions.

items.name: Tangency condition gives constant c + Point of tangency coordinates
items.how: Hence find the coordinates of the point of intersection.
items.ms: M1 solve the quadratic x^2 - 7x - c = 0 with their c (a repeated root x = 7/2), dM1 find y for their x, A1 (7/2, 7/4). A correct answer with correct c scores all three marks if no incorrect working is seen.

items.name: Obtuse angle by sine rule + Perimeter of sector and triangle shape
items.how: Hence find the perimeter of shape ABCDA to 1 d.p.
items.ms: M1 arc ABC = 6(2pi - 0.7) = 33.50, M1 length OD by the sine rule with angle OAD = 0.7 subtracted from pi less 2.258 (or the cosine rule and a quadratic in OD), giving about 1.42, ddM1 perimeter 33.50 + 5 + (6 - 1.42), A1 awrt 43.1.

items.name: Sketch 1 + sin and tan curves + Count solutions of trig equation graphically
items.how: Hence find the number of solutions of tan(theta) = 1 + sin(theta) in (i) a long interval (a whole number of 360 degree periods) and (ii) a second interval that omits part of the first.
items.ms: (i) M1 for the number of intersections per period (2) times the number of periods (6), A1 12; (ii) B1ft 11, or a follow-through of their (i) minus the solutions in the omitted section. If graphs are missing, 12 and 11 still earn their marks.
path: P1.3.3 - Sine, cosine and tangent fun

items.name: Expand cubic and differentiate + Show horizontal tangent at stationary point
items.how: Hence show that the equation of the tangent to the curve where x = 2.5 can be expressed in the form y = k, and find k.
items.ms: M1 evaluate f'(2.5) for their f', A1 show f'(2.5) = 12(2.5)^2 - 24(2.5) - 15 = 0 with embedded values (needs a correct f'), A1 cso y coordinate -54 so the tangent is y = -54. Solving f'(x) = 0 to get x = -0.5 and 2.5 is accepted for the first two marks.

items.name: Differentiate power terms and find normal
items.how: Single question (stem text missing from the input): (a) differentiate a curve given as power terms (x^2, x^(-1/2), x^(-1) and a constant); (b) find the equation of the normal at the point (4, 3) in the form ax + by + c = 0.
items.ms: (a) M1 reduce the power on any term (constant to 0), then A1 A1 A1 for one, two, then all three terms of dy/dx = (2/3)x - 2x^(-3/2) - (8/3)x^(-2) (no isw in this part). (b) M1 substitute x = 4 into their derivative (9/4), M1 perpendicular gradient -4/9, dM1 line through (4, 3) with the changed gradient (y = mx + c must reach c), A1 4x + 9y - 43 = 0 or an integer multiple.

items.name: Show relation using cosine rule
items.how: Triangle ABC with AB = p m, AC = q m, BC = 2root2 m and angle BAC = 60 degrees; show that p^2 + q^2 - pq = 8 (all stages).
items.ms: M1 cosine rule (2root2)^2 = p^2 + q^2 - 2pq*cos60 (or a perpendicular from B giving two right triangles), A1* the given result with cos60 replaced by 1/2 and no bracket errors; stating = 8 without any working scores no A mark.
path: P1.3.1 - The sine and cosine rules, a

items.name: Integrate product over root term
items.how: Find the integral of (3x + 2)(root x - 5)/(4*root x) with respect to x (stem partly lost in the input, reconstructed from the scheme), writing each term in simplest form.
items.ms: M1 write as a sum of terms using a correct index law at least once, A1 two correct terms, A1 all four ((3/4)x - (15/4)x^(1/2) + 1/2 - (5/2)x^(-1/2)), dM1 raise a power by one, A1 two terms correct and processed, A1 (3/8)x^2 - (5/2)x^(3/2) + x/2 - 5x^(1/2) + C on one line, all simplified. Unprocessed indices such as x^(1.5-0.5) lose marks.
path: P1.5.2 - Integration of xn and relate

items.name: Difference in model values at start
items.how: Share value models P_A = 53 - 0.4(t - 8)^2 and P_B = -1.6t + 44.2 (millions of pounds, t years); find the difference between the two values when monitoring began.
items.ms: M1 substitute t = 0 into P_A and take the difference from 44.2, A1 awrt 16.8 (million pounds).

items.name: Maximum of quadratic share model
items.how: State the maximum share value of company A during the 15-year period.
items.ms: B1 for 53 (million pounds), read from the turning point form of the model; units may be omitted.

items.name: Times when one model exceeds another
items.how: Find, using algebra and showing working, the times in the 15-year period when the share value of company A exceeded that of company B.
items.ms: M1 set -1.6t + 44.2 = 53 - 0.4(t - 8)^2 (an inequality sign is also accepted), M1 rearrange to 0.4t^2 - 8t + 84/5 = 0 and solve, A1 t = 10 - root58 = awrt 2.38, A1ft 2.38 < t <= 15 (upper limit from the model domain; follow through allowed).
path: P1.1.9 - Solutions of linear and quad

items.name: Limitation of quadratic model
items.how: Explain why the model for company A should not be used to predict its share value when t = 20.
items.ms: B1 for stating the predicted share value would be negative, or that the model is only known to hold for 15 years (20 is outside). Only '-4.6 < 0' is insufficient since it does not refer to the model or share value.

items.name: Tangent equation from derivative
items.how: Curve y = f(x), x > 0 passes through P(8, 2) with f'(x) = 32/(3x^2) + 3 - 2x^(1/3) (reconstructed from the scheme); find the equation of the tangent at P in the form y = mx + c.

items.name: Integrate derivative to find f
items.how: Find f(x), in simplest form, from f'(x) and the point P(8, 2).

path: P1.5.2 - Integration of xn and relate

items.name: y-intercept of a line
items.how: Line l1 has equation 4y + 3x = 48 and cuts the y-axis at C; state the y coordinate of C.
items.ms: B1 for 12 (if the diagram and the working conflict, the main solution takes precedence).

(ii) B1 sqrt(27) = 3 sqrt(3), M1 rationalise the denominator by multiplying by (sqrt(3) - 1), M1 rearrange for a reaching a two-term expression, A1cso a = -(4/3) sqrt(3) + 8/3. items.name: Quadratic from roots and minimum point

items.ms: M1 f(x) = kx(x - 4) (or k(x-2)^2 - 4.8); dM1 use (2, -4.8) to find k; A1 f(x) = 1.2x(x - 4) or an equivalent expanded or completed-square form.

items.name: Cubic with repeated root through a point

items.name: Exponential sketch, trapezium rule, derived estimates
items.how: (a) Sketch y = a^(-x) + 4 with a > 1, showing the y-axis intersection and the asymptote equation (3 marks). (b) Using the trapezium rule with all six y-values of y = 3^(-x/2) + 4 in the table, estimate the integral from -4 to 8.5 to 2 s.f. (3 marks). (c) Using (b), estimate (i) the integral of 3^(-x/2) over the same interval and (ii) the sum of two integrals, one of 3^(-x/2) + 4 and one of its reflection in the y-axis (3 marks).
items.ms: (a) B1 decaying exponential shape in quadrants 1 and 2 not touching the x-axis, B1 intercept (0, 5), B1 asymptote y = 4 as an equation. (b) B1 h = 2.5, M1 (h/2){13 + 4.009 + 2(sum of the four middle values)}, A1 awrt 69 (a calculator integral, 66.4, scores 0). (c)(i) M1 subtract the rectangle, 4 x 12.5 = 50, A1ft awrt 19; (ii) B1ft awrt 138 = 2 x (b).

items.name: Log equation to cubic; solve
items.how: (a) Given 2log4(x + 3) + log4(x) = log4(4x + 2) + 1/2 (form read from the scheme), show that x^3 + 6x^2 + x - 4 = 0 (4 marks). (b) Given -1 is a root, (i) use algebra to find the other two roots (3 marks) and (ii) hence solve the logarithmic equation (1 mark).
items.ms: (a) B1 power law 2log4(x+3) = log4((x+3)^2) or 1/2 = log4(2), M1 combine at least two log terms, A1 log-free equation x(x+3)^2 = 2(4x+2), A1* expand to the given cubic with brackets multiplied out. (b)(i) M1 divide by (x + 1) to x^2 + 5x - 4, dM1 solve the quadratic, A1 x = (-5 +/- sqrt(41))/2. (ii) B1 x = (-5 + sqrt(41))/2 only, as logs need positive arguments.

items.name: Arithmetic model: wheat in year 4
items.how: A farm produces 300 tonnes of wheat in year 1 and is predicted to produce 4000 tonnes in year 12. Using model A (the same amount added each year), find the production in year 4 to the nearest 10 tonnes.
items.ms: M1 4000 = 300 + 11d and solve for d (about 336); M1 300 + 3d; A1 awrt 1310 tonnes. Using 12d instead of 11d gives 1225 and loses the A mark.

items.name: Geometric model: wheat in year 2
items.how: Using model B (the same percentage increase each year), find the production in year 2 to the nearest 10 tonnes.
items.ms: M1 4000 = 300 r^11 and solve for r (about 1.266); M1 multiply 300 by their r (needs r found from the equation); A1 awrt 380 tonnes.

items.name: Difference of totals under two models
items.how: Calculate, according to the two models, the difference between the total amounts of wheat produced from year 1 to year 12 inclusive, to the nearest 10 tonnes.
items.ms: M1 a correct sum formula for either series ((12/2)(300 + 4000) for the AP, 300(r^12 - 1)/(r - 1) for the GP); dM1 both attempted correctly and the difference taken (25800 - 17935); A1 7860 (7870 allowed, not awrt). A rounded r = 1.266 gives 7810 and loses the A mark.

items.name: Counterexample and proof by exhaustion
items.how: (i) Use a counter example to show that 'n^2 + 3n + 1 is prime for all n in the natural numbers' is false (2 marks). (ii) Use algebra to prove by exhaustion that n^2 - 2 is not a multiple of 4 for all natural n (4 marks).
items.ms: (i) M1 substitute a value giving a composite, e.g. n = 6, A1 correct calculation (55) with a conclusion that it is not prime. (ii) M1 n = 2p + 1 or n = 2p, expand n^2 - 2; A1 one case correct with a reason (4p^2 + 4p - 1 is one less than a multiple of 4); dM1 both odd and even cases; A1* both reasons (4p^2 - 2 is not a multiple of 4) and an overall conclusion, using a letter other than n.

items.name: Trig equation and sinusoidal graph points
items.how: Show detailed reasoning, no calculator-only solutions. (i) Solve sin x tan x = 5 for 0 <= x < 360 degrees, 1 d.p. (6 marks). (ii) Figure 1 shows y = A sin(2 theta - 3pi/8) + 2 (equation partly lost; form read from the scheme) with points P, Q, R and P having y-coordinate 7: (a) state A (1 mark); (b) find the exact coordinates of Q (3 marks); (c) find theta at R to 3 s.f. (4 marks).
items.ms: (i) B1 tan = sin/cos, M1 sin^2 = 1 - cos^2 to a quadratic in cos, A1 cos^2 x + 5cos x - 1 = 0, M1 solve, dM1 arccos in range, A1 x = 78.9 and 281.1 degrees. (ii)(a) B1 A = 5. (b) M1 solve 2theta - 3pi/8 = 3pi/2 for the minimum, A1 theta = 15pi/16, B1ft y = -3. (c) M1 set 5sin(2theta - 3pi/8) + 2 = 0 so sin = -2/5, dM1 arcsin and solve for theta, A1 a correct value from the family of solutions, A1 theta = awrt 5.51 radians.

items.name: Show stationary point has x-coordinate 9
items.how: Show detailed reasoning. Figure 2 shows a curve for x > 0 with terms in x^2 and x^(-3/2) (equation partly lost) and a single stationary point P. Use calculus to show that the x-coordinate of P is 9.
items.ms: M1 differentiate with at least one index correct; A1 dy/dx = x - 2187x^(-5/2) with indices processed; dM1 set to 0 and solve x^(7/2) = 2187 (or substitute x = 9 and show 0); A1* x = 9 reached with an intermediate step such as x = 2187^(2/7). Going straight from the equation to 9 is dM0A0.

items.name: Exact area using integration with line
items.how: Line l passes through P parallel to the x-axis. Use algebraic integration to find the exact area of region R, bounded by the curve, the line l and the line x = 4.
items.ms: M1 integrate with one index correct; A1ft x^3/6 - 2916x^(-1/2) - 74x (or the curve minus line integrated); B1 y at P = 20.5; dM1 full method: integral from 4 to 9 minus the rectangle (9 - 4)(20.5), with limits substituted; A1 373/3 (124 1/3) exact. No integration seen, or no evidence of limits, loses the method marks.

items.name: Show recurrence sequence is periodic + Order of periodic sequence + Sum of 70 terms of periodic sequence

items.name: Periodic sequence terms and 200-term sum

items.ms: (a) B1 a_2 = 1 and B1 a_107 = 3 (sequence alternates, period 2). (b) M1 sum of two distinct terms as 100(a + b) with allowable terms, A1 600. Using AP or GP formulae scores 0; slips such as 2a_n + 1 (terms 3, 7) or a wrong first value lose the A mark.

items.name: Maximum annual profit using calculus

items.name: Range where f is increasing

items.ms: M1 A1 f'(x) = -72/x^3 + 2, dM1 set f'(x) = 0 (or an inequality) and solve x^n = k with k > 0, A1 x > cube root of 36 in exact form (3.302 implies the first three marks).

items.name: Show definite integral equals zero
items.how: Show that a definite integral of 36/x^2 + 2x - 13 equals 0 (the printed integral is damaged; limits 2 and 9 by the scheme).
items.ms: M1 A1 integrate to -36/x + x^2 - 13x (indices processed, + c allowed), dM1 substitute the limits and subtract, A1* both values (-40) shown so the result is 0 with correct bracketing.

items.name: Integral with reversed limits and constant k
items.how: Given that the integral of f(x) from x = 2 to x = 6 is -8: (i) state the value of the integral from 6 to 2; (ii) find the constant k such that the integral from 2 to 6 of (36/x^2 + 2x + k) is 0.
items.ms: (i) B1 8. (ii) M1 integrate all terms with kx, apply limits 2 and 6 and set the linear expression in k to 0 (or note the curve must rise 2 units, or solve -8 + 4(k + 13) = 0), A1 k = -11 (minus sign lost in the extract; 11 in magnitude).

items.name: Factor theorem to show k equals 9 + Fully factorise the cubic
items.how: Using algebra and showing each step, fully factorise f(x) = 9x^3 - 15x^2 - 32x - 12 (the scheme treats this as a 'Hence' part although the word is missing from the extract).
items.ms: M1 divide or factorise out (x - 3), A1 quadratic factor 9x^2 + 12x + 4, dM1 factorise the quadratic, A1 (x - 3)(3x + 2)^2 as a product. Writing roots or factors with no working scores at most the special-case 1010 or nothing.

items.name: Show trig equation reduces to quadratic in cos + Solve trig equation in 2x
items.how: Hence solve cos(2x) - 1 = 4 sin(2x) tan(2x) over a given interval in radians (0 to pi/2 by the scheme's solutions), giving answers where appropriate to 2 d.p.
items.ms: M1 solve the quadratic ((5cos2x + 4)(cos2x - 1) = 0), A1 critical values cos2x = -4/5 and 1, dM1 correct method for x from cos2x = -4/5 (including halving), A1 x = 0 and 1.25 with no other values in range.

items.name: Arithmetic sequence nth term; weeks to reach total
items.how: No parts and no wording in the extract; per the scheme: (a)(i) decide whether the given terms (first term 5, common difference 0.25) suit an arithmetic or geometric series, (ii) give the nth term; (b) use the sum formula to find how many weeks until the total reaches 350.
items.ms: (a) B1 identifies a common difference so arithmetic, M1 nth term with n or n - 1, A1 5 + 0.25(n - 1). (b) M1 A1 S_n = (n/2)(2 x 5 + (n - 1) x 0.25) against 350, M1 solve the 3-term quadratic (0.25n^2 + 9.75n = 700), A1 37 weeks selected. Geometric formulae earn only partial credit; listing attempts go to review.

items.name: Proof by contradiction cube root of 2 irrational

items.how: Two independent parts (show all stages, no calculator reliance): (i) use u = e^x - 3 to show the integral of 4e^(3x)/(e^x - 3) from ln 5 to ln 7 equals a + b ln 2; (ii) show by integration that the integral of 3e^x cos 2x dx = p e^x sin 2x + q e^x cos 2x + c, finding p and q.

items.ms: M1 attempts to solve one of the remaining factor pairs, A1 one case correctly solved, dM1 solves both remaining cases (3x - y = 25, x + y = 1 gives x = 6.5, y = -5.5; 3x - y = 5, x + y = 5 gives x = 2.5, y = 2.5), A1 all correct with the reason (not integers) and a concluding statement; including factor pairs that do not multiply to 25 loses the last mark.

items.name: Integration by parts and by substitution

(ii) B1 substitution and differential (u = 2x-1 most common), M1 integrand fully in u, A1 correct integrand, dM1 integrate to p ln u + q/u form, A1 correct integration, M1 changed limits (or back-substitute), A1 3/20 + ln 4; avoiding substitution scores the special case B0M0A0 then M1A1dM1A1.

items.name: Contradiction proof that k + 9/k >= 6

items.ms: B1 driving force 3P/12, M1A1 constant-speed equation up the hill, M1A1A1 equation of motion down the hill with P/12 (at most one error then correct), dM1 solve the simultaneous equations, A1 P = 4500, A1 R = 525 (530); misreading weight as mass loses marks (SC).

items.name: Exact tan theta for rod, two rough surfaces
items.how: Find the exact value of tan theta for a uniform 25 kg, 3 m rod AB with A on rough ground and B against a rough wall (two given coefficients of friction), in limiting equilibrium; figure given.
items.ms: B1 F = mu R used at least once, M1A1 resolve horizontally, M1A1 resolve vertically, M1A1 a moments equation (any pivot), dM1 substitute to get an equation in tan theta only, A1 tan theta = 13/40 (0.325); friction in the wrong direction gives A0.

items.name: Centre of mass of square lamina with holes
items.how: Show that G is 42a/11 from AD for lamina L formed by removing a square (side 2a) and a square (side 4a) from an 8a square ABCD; figure with positions given.
items.ms: B1 mass ratios 64 : 4 : 16 : 44, B1 distances from AD (4a, 2a, 5a), M1 moments about AD or a parallel axis, A1 correct unsimplified equation, A1* d = 42a/11.
path: M2.2.2 - Centre of mass of uniform pl

items.name: Suspended lamina with particle at C
items.how: A particle kM is attached at C and the lamina hangs freely from B with BC at 45 deg to the horizontal; find k.
items.ms: B1 combined centre of mass on the line through B at 45 deg (midpoint of the diagonal), M1 moments (about B, the midpoint of AB or the centre), A1 correct unsimplified equation, A1 k = 1/22 (0.05 or better).

deps.name: Centre of mass of square lamina with holes

items.name: Acceleration from velocity vector at t=3
items.how: Find the acceleration of P at t = 3 given v = (3t^2 - 9t + 6)i + (t^2 + t - 6)j.
items.ms: M1 differentiate v (powers down by 1), A1 a = (6t - 9)i + (2t + 1)j, A1 9i + 7j.
path: Topic 1 Kinematics of a particle moving in a straight line or plane

items.name: Distance OA at instantaneous rest
items.how: P is at O when t = 0 and comes to instantaneous rest at A; find the distance OA.
items.ms: M1A1 set both components of v to zero (factorise) giving t = 2, M1A1A1 integrate v for r (at most one error, then correct), dM1 substitute t = 2 and use Pythagoras, A1 (2/3)sqrt130 = 7.6 or better.
path: Topic 1 Kinematics of a particle moving in a straight line or plane

items.name: Work done against friction along ramp
items.how: Find the work done against friction as a 6 kg particle (mu = 0.25) is projected up a 15 m rough ramp (tan alpha given, 5/12 by the scheme).
items.ms: B1 R = 6g cos alpha, M1 work done = 15 x 0.25 x R, A1 204 J (or 200 J, 21g).

items.name: Speeds at top of ramp and landing
items.how: Use the work-energy principle to find (i) the speed v at the top B of the ramp and (ii) the speed w when P hits the ground at C after leaving B as a projectile.
items.ms: M1 work-energy for v (dimensionally correct), A1ft at most one error, A1ft correct, A1 v = 3.88; M1 work-energy for w, A1ft, A1 w = 11.3; suvat is not accepted as the question specifies work-energy.

deps.name: Work done against friction along ramp

items.name: Coefficient of restitution from KE gain
items.how: A (3m, speed 2u) hits B (m, speed u, same direction) and B's direction is unchanged; given the KE gained by B, find the coefficient of restitution.
items.ms: M1A1 KE gain for B to find its speed (11u/5), M1A1 CLM 3m x 2u + mu = 3mv + mw (v = 8u/5), M1A1 impact law w - v = e(2u - u), dM1 solve for e, A1 e = 3/5.
path: M2.4.2 - Direct impact of elastic par

items.name: Coefficient of restitution at wall
items.how: B hits a smooth wall (coefficient f) and its speed afterwards equals A's speed after the first collision; find f.
items.ms: M1 impact law fw = v (sign error condoned), A1 f = 8/11 (0.73 or better), positive.

deps.name: Coefficient of restitution from KE gain

items.how: A ball projected from O with (pi + qj) passes A at t = 3 s with velocity (8i - 12j); find the speed at projection.
items.ms: B1 p = 8, M1 suvat for the vertical component -12 = q - 3g, A1 q = 17.4, M1 Pythagoras for the speed (independent), A1 19.2 (19) m/s.

items.name: Height of B above A, perpendicular directions
items.how: At B the direction of motion is perpendicular to that at A; find the vertical height of B above A.
items.ms: M1 vertical component of velocity at B from perpendicularity (2/3 x 8), A1 16/3, dM1 suvat or energy between A and B with -12 and 16/3, A1 h = 5.9 (max 3 s.f.).
path: Topic 1 Kinematics of a particle moving in a straight line or plane

items.name: Work-energy down a rough inclined plane
items.how: Two-part question (question text missing from the input, reconstructed from the scheme): (a) show that the work done against friction over a distance d equals a given multiple of mgd, (b) find the speed after that distance using the work-energy principle; the scheme uses mu = 1/5 and a slope with cos = 12/13, sin = 5/13.
items.ms: (a) B1 for R = mg cos(alpha), M1 for work done = friction x distance, A1* for the printed 12/65 mgd from correct working; (b) M1 work-energy equation with all terms dimensionally correct (sign errors condoned), A1 with at most one error, A1 correct unsimplified, A1 for v = sqrt(2gd/5), about 0.63 sqrt(gd).

items.name: Engine power from two slope motions
items.how: Find the value of P for a 450 kg vehicle on an inclined road (the value of sin theta is lost in the input; the scheme uses 1/15), moving at 12 m/s down the slope with power P and acceleration 0.5, then up the slope with power 2P and deceleration 0.5, with constant resistance R.
items.ms: M1 A1 A1 equation of motion down the slope (at most one error, then fully correct, in P or F1); M1 A1 equation of motion up the slope with consistent signs and the change of direction; M1 for P = Fv used at least once; DM1 solve the simultaneous equations for P (R eliminated); A1 P = 1660 or 1700 (2 or 3 sf with g = 9.8). Marks are lost through sign errors for resistance/gravity or by forgetting that the engine force is 2P/12 in the second case.

items.name: Instantaneous rest times from displacement function
items.how: Particle on the x-axis with x given as a polynomial in t (partly garbled in the input); find the non-zero values of t at which P is at instantaneous rest.
items.ms: M1 differentiate x to obtain v; DM1 set v = 0 and solve (factorise out the factor t, then the quadratic); A1 t = 1 and t = 4 (correct solution only). The root t = 0 must be excluded and both roots given.
path: Topic 1 Kinematics of a particle moving in a straight line or plane

items.name: Total distance with change of direction
items.how: Find the total distance travelled by P in 0 <= t <= 4 for the displacement function given in the stem.
items.ms: M1 correct strategy: split the interval at the turning point t = 1 and sum |x(1) - x(0)| + |x(4) - x(1)|; A1ft correct unsimplified expression for their turning points; A1 distance = 56 m (cso). The usual error is to use x(4) - x(0) and ignore the change of direction.

deps.name: Instantaneous rest times from displacement function

path: Topic 1 Kinematics of a particle moving in a straight line or plane

items.name: Acceleration at a given time
items.how: Find the acceleration of P when t = 4, from the same displacement function.
items.ms: M1 differentiate v to get a (a = dv/dt); M1 substitute t = 4 into their a and simplify; A1 a = 42 m s^-2 (correct solution only).
path: Topic 1 Kinematics of a particle moving in a straight line or plane

items.name: Impulse in vector form, two values
items.how: Find the two possible values of the constant c, given a 0.75 kg particle with velocity 4i receiving an impulse J = c(-i + 2j) and having speed 8 m/s afterwards.
items.ms: M1 I = m(v - u) as a vector equation; A1 correct substituted form for v; M1 Pythagoras with the speed 8; A1 correct unsimplified equation in c; M1 simplify to the 3-term quadratic 5c^2 - 6c - 27 = 0 and solve; A1 c = 3 and c = -9/5 (both required). A vector-triangle plus cosine rule method earns the same marks.
path: M2.4.1 - Momentum as a vector. The im

items.name: Cable tension by moments about B
items.how: Show that the tension in the cable is 56 N for a uniform pole AB (length 2.5 m, weight 70 N) resting against a rough wall and held by a 4 m cable, given tan alpha.
items.ms: M1 moments about B (dimensionally correct, forces resolved) or a correct moments plus resolution approach; A1 unsimplified equation in alpha with at most one error (e.g. T x 2.5 sin(alpha) = 70 x 1.25 sin(2 alpha)); A1 correct unsimplified equation with trig evaluated; A1* T = 56 N from exact working with no errors.

items.name: Coefficient of friction for limiting rod
items.how: Given the pole is in limiting equilibrium, find the coefficient of friction between the pole and the wall.
items.ms: M1 A1ft resolve horizontally (H = T sin alpha, the normal reaction); M1 A1ft resolve vertically (V + T cos alpha = 70, V is the friction); M1 F = mu R with their V and H; A1 mu = 3/4. A resolution parallel and perpendicular to the rod is an accepted alternative. Marks are lost by treating the vertical force as the normal reaction at the wall.

deps.name: Cable tension by moments about B

items.name: Coefficient of restitution from impulse on A
items.how: Find the coefficient of restitution between A (mass 2m) and B (mass 3m) which collide directly while moving in opposite directions, given they move apart at equal speed v afterwards and A receives an impulse of magnitude 5mv.
items.ms: M1 A1 impulse on A, 5mv = 2m(v - (-x)), giving the speed of A before impact x = 3v/2; M1 A1 impulse on B (or conservation of momentum) giving y = 2v/3; M1 A1 Newton's law of restitution with the speeds before and after impact; e = 12/13 (0.92 or better).
path: M2.4.2 - Direct impact of elastic par

items.name: Wall coefficient of restitution from kinetic energy loss
items.how: Find f, the coefficient of restitution between B and a fixed wall, given that the total kinetic energy lost by B (in the collision with A and with the wall) is E and the kinetic energy lost by A is 2E.
items.ms: B1 speed of B after the wall = vf; M1 kinetic energy equation relating B's total loss to half of A's loss using the speeds before collision from (a) (change in KE condoned); A1 correct unsimplified equation in f; A1 f = 1/6 (cao).

deps.name: Coefficient of restitution from impulse on A

items.how: Show that a equals a given multiple of d for a uniform lamina formed from rectangle ABCE and a sector CDE of angle pi/6, given its centre of mass lies on EC (formulae book sector result may be used).
items.ms: B1 centre of mass of the sector at 2a sin(alpha)/(3 alpha) = 2a/pi from C seen or implied; M1 moments about EC (dimensionally correct, parallel axis condoned); A1 correct unsimplified equation; A1* the printed relation from correct working.

items.name: Angle of suspended composite lamina from B
items.how: Find beta in radians, the angle BC makes with the downward vertical when the lamina hangs freely from B.
items.ms: B1 mass (area) ratios of rectangle and sector; M1 moments about BC (dimensionally correct); A1ft correct unsimplified equation using the a-d relation from (a); A1 distance of the centre of mass from BC; M1 trig for the angle with the vertical; A1ft correct unsimplified equation; A1 beta = 0.74 (0.737) or better (42.2 degrees implies the method).

deps.name: Composite lamina centre of mass on EC

items.name: Height of projection by conservation of energy
items.how: By considering energy, find h, the height of A above the ground, for a particle projected at 10 m/s which hits the ground at 18 m/s.
items.ms: M1 conservation of energy with all three terms dimensionally correct (sign errors condoned); A1 correct unsimplified equation 1/2 m(10^2) + mgh = 1/2 m(18^2); A1 h = 11.4 (3 sf or 2 sf).

items.name: Horizontal distance OB of projectile
items.how: Find the horizontal distance OB, given the particle takes 2.5 s to reach the ground from the projection point at height h.
items.ms: M1 complete suvat method on the vertical motion to find the angle of projection; A1ft equation 10 sin(alpha) x 2.5 - g(2.5^2)/2 = -h (follow their h); A1 alpha about 50.2 degrees; M1 horizontal distance = 10 cos(alpha) x 2.5; A1 OB = 16.0 m (3 sf or 2 sf).

deps.name: Height of projection by conservation of energy

items.ms: (a) M1 moments about the y-axis with all terms (m may be omitted), A1* printed result; (b) M1 moments about the x-axis, A1 y-bar = (1 + 4k)/9, DM1 substitute x-bar and y-bar into x + 2y = 3 and solve for k, A1 k = 23/20.

items.name: Acceleration of car under constant power
items.how: Find the acceleration of a 900 kg car travelling down a slope (sin alpha = 1/12 in the scheme) at 16 m/s with the engine at a constant 15 kW and a constant 400 N resistance.
items.ms: M1 P = Fv with 15000 and 16 (F = 937.5 N); M1 equation of motion along the slope with all terms (sign errors and sin/cos confusion condoned); A1 unsimplified with at most one error; A1 correct unsimplified equation with F substituted; A1 a = 1.41 (1.4) m s^-2.

items.name: Impulse giving two possible values of lambda
items.how: Find the possible values of lambda, given a 0.2 kg particle with velocity (4i - 3j) receives an impulse lambda(i + j) and then has speed 7 m/s.
items.ms: M1 I = mv - mu; A1 correct vector equation 0.2(v - (4i - 3j)) = lambda(i + j); M1 Pythagoras with 49; A1 correct unsimplified equation; DM1 form and solve the quadratic in lambda; A1 lambda = 3/5 or -4/5. Treating 7 as a vector gets no marks unless recovered; a vector triangle with the cosine rule is an alternative.
path: M2.4.1 - Momentum as a vector. The im

items.name: Acceleration when velocity is parallel to i
items.how: Find the acceleration of P at t = lambda, the instant when its velocity (an i component with a square root of 5 - t and a quadratic j component) is parallel to i.
items.ms: M1 set the j component to zero and solve for lambda; A1 lambda = 1; M1 differentiate both components with respect to t (square root handled by the chain rule); A1 any equivalent vector form for a; A1 a = -1/4 i + 4j (isw if the magnitude follows).
path: Topic 1 Kinematics of a particle moving in a straight line or plane

items.name: Position vector by integrating velocity
items.how: Find, in terms of T, the position vector of P at t = T (1 <= T < 5), given the position vector at t = 1.
items.ms: M1 integrate both components (powers go up); A1 unsimplified with at most one error; A1 correct integral (constants optional); DM1 use t = 1, r = -2i + j to find the constants; A1 r = (-(2/3)(5 - T)^(3/2) + 10/3)i + (T^3/3 + T^2 - 3T + 8/3)j.
path: Topic 1 Kinematics of a particle moving in a straight line or plane

items.name: Show AD length using right angle at contact
items.how: Show that AD = sqrt(29) a, for a rod AB resting on a smooth hemisphere (centre D, radius 2a) at C where AC = 5a.
items.ms: B1* correct use of Pythagoras in the right-angled triangle ACD (radius perpendicular to the rod at C): AD^2 = (2a)^2 + (5a)^2, with a on both sides.

items.name: Normal reaction at C by moments
items.how: Show that the normal reaction at C between the rod and the block has magnitude 4W/sqrt(29).
items.ms: M1 moments about A (dimensionally correct, a may cancel; sin/cos confusion condoned); A1 correct unsimplified equation W x 4a cos(theta) = N x 5a with cos(theta) = 5/sqrt(29); A1* printed result from correct working.

deps.name: Show AD length using right angle at contact

items.name: Hinge force magnitude and direction
items.how: Find (i) the exact value of k and (ii) the exact value of tan(alpha), where the resultant force at the hinge A has magnitude kW and acts at angle alpha to the ground.
items.ms: M1 A1 resolve vertically (V + N cos(theta) = W); M1 A1 resolve horizontally (H = N sin(theta)); DM1 Pythagoras for k; A1 k = sqrt(145)/29 (a decimal alone is A0); DM1 trig for tan(alpha); A1 tan(alpha) = 9/8. Moments about C or resolving along and perpendicular to the rod are accepted alternatives.

deps.name: Show AD length using right angle at contact

items.ms: M1 A1 conservation of momentum 5u = vA + 2vB; M1 A1 Newton's law of restitution vB - vA = e(3u - u); DM1 solve for vA or vB; A1* vB = (5 + 2e)u/3 shown; A1 vA = (5 - 4e)u/3 (must be positive).

items.name: Time between collisions with wall rebound
items.how: Find T in terms of d and u, the time between the first and second collisions of A and B, given e = 1/2, B rebounds from a smooth wall (coefficient of restitution 1/3 in the scheme) and the first collision is at distance d from the wall.
items.ms: B1 time for B to reach the wall d/(2u); B1 speed of B after the wall (2u/3); M1 distance travelled by A before B hits the wall (d/2); M1 closing-time formula with the correct relative speeds; A1 correct unsimplified equation; A1 T = 4d/(5u). items.ms: M1 P = Fv (F = 500/6); M1 equation of motion F - 60 = 80a; A1 correct unsimplified equation in F; A1 a = 7/24 (0.29 or better) m s^-2.

items.name: Total work done by cyclist up hill
items.how: Find the total work done by the cyclist from A to B (20 km up a slope rising 300 m, starting from rest and ending at 8 m/s) with a constant 60 N non-gravitational resistance.
items.ms: B1 B1 gain in KE (1/2 x 80 x 8^2) and gain in GPE (80 x 9.8 x 300), one mark per correct term; M1 combined work-energy expression with all terms and no double counting (suvat with F = ma scores M0); A1 correct unsimplified expression including work against resistance 60 x 20000; A1 about 1440 kJ (1400 kJ); joules accepted.

items.name: Power for constant speed uphill
items.how: Find P, the constant power needed for the cyclist to climb a slope (sin(alpha) = 1/20 in the scheme) at a steady 7 m/s with 60 N non-gravitational resistance.
items.ms: M1 equation of motion along the slope with the driving force, 60 N and 80g sin(alpha) (zero resultant); A1 unsimplified equation in P or F with at most one error; A1 correct unsimplified equation in P using F = P/7; A1 P = 694 (690) W.

items.name: Tension in string by moments about hinge
items.how: Show that T = 6W/5, the tension in a string holding a uniform rod AB (weight W, hinged at A, a particle attached at B) in equilibrium; the weight of the particle appears as W/4 in the scheme.
items.ms: M1 moments about A with all terms and forces resolved (M0 if no resolving); A1 correct unsimplified equation; A1* T = 6W/5 with cancelling or simplification shown.

items.name: Magnitude of hinge force on rod
items.how: Find, in terms of W, the magnitude of the force exerted on the rod by the hinge at A.
items.ms: Two independent equations (resolve horizontally and vertically, or moments about B or C, or along/perpendicular to the rod): M1 A1 for the first and M1 A1 for the second, e.g. H = T cos 30, V + T cos 60 = rod and particle weights; DM1 Pythagoras for R; A1 R = (sqrt(601)/20)W, about 1.2W.

items.name: Position, acceleration and timing from velocity vector

items.ms: (a) M1 integrate v, A1 correct integration, DM1 use the initial position to find the constant (or a definite integral) and substitute t = 3, A1 r = 87i + 45j; (b) M1 differentiate v, A1 a = (6t + 12)i + (10t + 10)j, DM1 substitute t = 3 and use Pythagoras, A1 50 m s^-2; (c) M1 equation in T from the ratio of components of v, A1 T = 6/7 (0.86).

items.ms: M1 A1 impulse = change in momentum as a vector (3(x - 5)i + 3yj); M1 Pythagoras with |I|^2 = 9 x 82; M1 A1 change in KE 1/2 x 3(x^2 + y^2 - 25) = 138; DM1 solve the simultaneous equations; A1 v = 6i + 9j (A0 for poor notation or subtraction the wrong way round).

items.ms: M1 for attempting to rank the 200 m times (at least 3 correct), A1 for both rankings correct, A1 for sum d^2 = 18, dM1 for the correct formula using their sum d^2, A1 for awrt 0.679.

items.name: One-tailed test for positive rank correlation
items.how: Stating hypotheses clearly, test at the 5% level for evidence of positive correlation between the two finishing orders.
items.ms: B1 for H0: rho = 0 and H1: rho > 0, B1 for the one-tailed critical value 0.7143, M1 for comparing their rs with their critical value, A1ft for a contextual conclusion (0.679 < 0.7143 so insufficient evidence of positive correlation between the finishing orders).

deps.name: Spearman's rank coefficient, race finishing orders

items.name: Spearman's coefficient with tied ranks

items.ms: B1 for noting tied lengths so average (shared) ranks are used, dependent B1 for then using the product moment formula Sxy/sqrt(SxxSyy) on those average ranks. Marks are lost by giving the standard 6 sum d^2 formula.
